summary: Round r1 (restricted network; data hosts blocked; one web search used). All empirical items are PENDING. Q1 (installed capacity, annual generation, wet/dry gap), Q2 (pipeline by status and historical completion rate) and Q3 (transmission corridors constraining evacuation and export) are designed but unanswered. Primary documents located: NEA annual reports and directorate publications (energy balance, monthly tables, capacity and transmission lists), DoED licence registers, MoF Economic Surveys FY2024/25 and FY2025/26, NRB and customs electricity trade tables (HS 2716), CEA cross-border approval page, 2018 guidelines and 2021 procedure, CEA National Electricity Plan (Transmission), CERC monthly/annual market reports and IEX price pages. Designed: (i) an INPS electricity balance per Nepal FY implemented with src.economic_model.energy.ElectricityBalance, with an explicit residual; (ii) a monthly seasonal profile on Nepali months aligned with 22B price seasons; (iii) a licence-cohort survival (Kaplan-Meier) completion-rate method with cancellations as failures; (iv) a transmission bottleneck register separating thermal rating, operational transfer limit and CEA-approved trading quantum. Reported 2026 events (Kyirong-Rasuwa flood, Indian approval decisions) are unverified and flagged.

findings.claim: Wet season defined on Nepali months as Jestha-Kartik (approximately mid-May to mid-November) and dry season as Mangsir-Baisakh, for alignment with NEA monthly tables; alternative definitions tested for sensitivity.
findings.note: Season boundaries are a modelling choice to be confirmed against NEA's own convention; coordinated with 22B price seasons.

findings.claim: Pipeline MW is not treated as future capacity; only completion-rate-weighted cohorts enter capacity paths, with climate (25A/22D) and market-access (25B) constraints as separate scenario parameters.
findings.note: Avoids the common practice of equating licensed MW with expected supply.

data_gaps: Every empirical value: no primary document could be downloaded in r1.
DoED historical licence registers including cancelled/expired licences (needed for unbiased completion rates) - availability unknown.
Project-level commissioning dates matched to licence records (NEA/DoED).
NEA monthly generation by plant and plant type (also requested by 22D); may need a data request to NEA system operation.
Operational transfer limits (N-1) of cross-border lines - may exist only in joint technical team minutes (CEA PSPA-II).
ERC Nepal is not in the source catalog; its URL is from general knowledge.
Final (not draft) CEA National Electricity Plan Vol II.

assumptions.text: Balance scope is INPS grid; off-grid and captive generation reported separately.
Season definition on Nepali months (wet = Jestha-Kartik); sensitivity to alternatives.
Completion rates estimated by licence cohort with cancellations as failures and right-censoring for open cohorts.
Three capacity notions for cross-border lines are never merged: thermal rating, operational transfer limit, approved trading quantum.
Media reports are pointers to primary documents only, never evidence.

challenges.text: Accepted: energy will be stored in GWh with explicit kWh conversion and Nepal FY. Proposed shared season basis: Nepali months (wet = Jestha-Kartik); 22B should re-aggregate IEX 15-minute prices to the same months.

NEA monthly generation by plant type is not confirmed to be published at plant level; 05A will request it from NEA (pending). Until then the flow-to-generation mapping should use plant-type aggregates.
Accepted: dry-season flow ranges (PR-05/PR-07) will enter as scenario sensitivities on the seasonal profile, not as a point path.
Accepted: the Indian 2018 guidelines' eligibility conditions and CEA approved quantum are modelled as a binding market-access constraint in the transmission register, separate from physical capacity.
Propose adding ERC Nepal (Electricity Regulatory Commission) as a tier-1 catalog source; and confirm document-level endpoints for doed.gov.np licence registers.

Hand-off: the export-vs-domestic comparison must use the seasonal surplus (wet-season spill/export) rather than annual averages; industrial demand in the dry season competes with imports, not exports.
Escalation: if reported 2026 events (Kyirong-Rasuwa damage to Trishuli corridor; Indian approval decisions) are verified, generation and export baselines in S05/S09 change.
Red-team note: India is the sole physical and regulatory export route and a dry-season supplier; approval decisions with hour limits are a two-way dependence to review.

uncertainty: High: no value retrieved. Structural uncertainties once data arrive: (i) NEA, customs and CERC trade volumes differ by metering point and period basis; (ii) IPP 'generation' is energy purchased at interconnection, not gross output; (iii) loss-rate base definitions vary; (iv) completion rates depend on whether cancelled licences are recorded; (v) cross-border 'capacity' has three distinct meanings; (vi) climate-driven dry-season flows and 2026 hazard events may shift the seasonal profile beyond historical ranges.

electricity_balance.identity: generation + imports = domestic_sales + exports + losses + own_use_residual (GWh)
electricity_balance.period_basis: Nepal FY (mid-July to mid-July); FY2015/16-FY2025/26. Indian-FY (April-March) CERC/CEA series only via monthly re-aggregation.
electricity_balance.scope: INPS (grid) only; captive/off-grid/solar-rooftop net metering reported separately if data exist

losses.definition_issue: NEA loss percentage base (net energy available vs gross incl. exports) to be recorded from report text

own_use_residual.method: closing residual; flagged if > tolerance and escalated to 00B

known_methodological_issues: NEA vs customs vs CERC trade volume differences (metering point, period basis, deviation settlement energy)
IPP generation reported as NEA purchase (energy delivered at interconnection) not gross generation

variables: monthly generation by plant type (ROR, PROR, storage, solar)

metrics.wet_dry_gap: (wet-season generation - dry-season generation) / annual generation; and dry-season net imports GWh
metrics.dry_season_deficit: max(0, domestic demand - domestic generation) per month
metrics.wet_season_surplus: max(0, domestic generation - domestic demand) per month, split into exported vs spilled

seasonal_profile.season_definition: wet = Jestha-Kartik; dry = Mangsir-Baisakh (assumption, sensitivity tested)

links.22B: price seasons aligned to the same monthly basis
links.22D: monthly generation by plant needed for flow-generation mapping (availability pending)
links.25A: dry-season flow ranges enter as scenario sensitivities

pipeline_completion_rate.definition: Share of generation-licensed capacity (MW) in licence cohort c that reaches commercial operation within k years of licence issue; reported as a survival (Kaplan-Meier) curve with right-censoring for cohorts still within their RCOD window
method: Build project-level panel from DoED generation-licence register (project, capacity, licence date, RCOD, cancellation) matched to NEA commissioning dates
Kaplan-Meier survival of 'not yet commissioned' by MW and by count; hazard by cohort, size class, ownership, basin, PPA status (take-or-pay vs other)
Cancelled/expired licences treated as failures, not censored
RCOD slippage distribution = actual COD - RCOD (years)
Apply cohort hazards to current under-construction and licensed stock to derive completion-weighted capacity paths; no point forecast, ranges only
pipeline_completion_rate.data_risk: DoED historical registers may only list current licences; cancelled licences may be missing, biasing completion rates upward

candidate_entries.corridor: Other existing lower-voltage cross-border radial links (e.g. Kataiya-Kusaha, Raxaul-Parwanipur, Tanakpur-Mahendranagar)
Inaruwa-New Purnea (planned, JV agreement reported Oct 2025)
Rasuwagadhi-Kerung (Nepal-China, proposed; exposed to reported 2026 Kyirong-Rasuwa event)

transmission_bottlenecks.note: Corridor names are candidate labels (general knowledge and media pointers) to be replaced by NEA/CEA nomenclature; no capacity values recorded in r1.
transmission_bottlenecks.bottleneck_test: A corridor is binding if connected + committed generation (completion-weighted) exceeds operational transfer limit in any wet-season month, or if CEA-approved quantum < exportable surplus.
